result.title: AutoHebb: Self-Modifying Neural Networks that Zero-Shot Infer and Continually Learn
result.summary: Humans and animals have a unique capacity to generalize and learn in novel circumstances, including "0-shot" inference (ZI) and continual learning (CL) -- two powerful cognitive abilities. Despite this importance, efforts to model ZI and CL are seriously limited in several ways. First, existing models typically lack components critical to ZI and CL in the brain, namely, strong inductive biases (for ZI) and autonomous control of learning (for CL). Second, models can be less tractable to analysis if model components are overly complex (lacking simplicity), or too task-restricted if model components are overly bespoke (lacking expressivity). Here we introduce autonomous Hebbian networks ("AutoHebb"), a class of online learning feedforward neural networks that realize strong inductive biases and autonomously controlled learning, and are both simple and expressive. Unlike standard models that learn via externally controlled optimization (e.g. gradient descent), AutoHebb networks combine external feedback with internally generated activity to produce a global learning signal ('neuromodulator') fed back to the network. The neuromodulator in turn gates a biologically grounded local learning rule (3-factor Hebbian rule) that updates networks' plastic weights. Using meta-learning to search for fixed (non-plastic) weights, we find that AutoHebb networks (1) succeed on ZI tasks, (2) show emergent (untrained) ZI/CL abilities, (3) admit reverse-engineering into explicit algorithms, and (4) outperform modern learning models on ZI/CL tasks. Lastly, performance comparisons to related models implied an essential role for three model components: meta-learning, Hebbian plasticity, and autonomous control of learning. These findings indicate that AutoHebb may be useful in hypothesis generation, analysis, and discovery of biologically grounded forms of learning and generalization.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 AutoHebb：一类在线学习的前馈网络，将外部反馈与内部生成的活动合成为全局「神经调质」信号，门控三因子 Hebbian 局部规则以更新可塑权重，并用元学习搜索固定权重；在零样本推断与持续学习任务上验证其有效，并尝试反推出显式算法。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉或多模态推理无直接联系，但其「内部活动生成学习信号、自主控制何时更新」的机制可能为 LVR 中的状态更新、动态计算与停止决策提供类比线索，可供核查。
